references.text: The context describes the richness of the promised land with water, wheat, barley, vineyards, fig trees, pomegranates, olive trees, and honey - all completing the picture of a land without lack.
Moses' blessing over Asher mentions iron and copper in connection with the land's resources, reflecting the description of mineral wealth in Deuteronomy 8:9.
Job describes how iron is taken from the earth and copper is smelted from stone, showing the practical use of the land's mineral resources.
The psalm assures that those who fear the Lord shall not lack any good thing, a theme reflecting the promise of a land where one shall not lack anything.
The Lord as shepherd ensures that one shall not lack anything - the same promise of abundance given in the description of the promised land.
Jesus teaches his disciples to pray for daily bread, linking to the promise that God's people would eat bread without lack in the promised land.
Jesus urges his disciples not to worry about food and clothing, for their heavenly Father knows what they need - an echo of God's care for His people in the wilderness and in the promised land.
